title: Fastest Production Cars in the World
metric_label: Top speed · VERIFIED one-way run or maker CLAIM
source_line: Sources: maker releases, independent timing (Racelogic, TÜV), press

items.name: Yangwang U9 Xtreme
items.subtitle: Papenburg, Germany
items.image_credit: BYD / Yangwang press photo (via Motoring Research)
items.image_hint: Yangwang U9 Xtreme (BYD), the 2025 record car with large rear wing; real photo of the actual car (Papenburg record run, Goodwood, Nürburgring or motor show), full car visible, 3/4 front or side; NOT Yangwang U8 SUV, not a render. If no Xtreme photo exists, a real photo of the standard Yangwang U9 coupe

source.name: BYD / Yangwang press release, 2025-09 (ATP Papenburg certified)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of production car speed records (excluded list, one-way run)

items.notes: Record car described as a prototype in Wikipedia's list (status not stated by BYD). First customer Xtreme delivered 2026-04-24 at Auto China (CnEVPost). 496.22 km/h on 2025-09-14 at ATP Automotive Testing Papenburg, driver Marc Basseng, one direction only (so not a Guinness two-way record). Xtreme = track-focused limited version of the U9 (max 30 units); U9 Track Edition specs filed with China's MIIT (road homologation filing). Standard U9 (on sale since Feb 2024, mass production Aug 2024) reached 391.94 km/h in 2024. Brand: Yangwang (BYD), China.
items.image_alt_credit: David Merrett / CC BY 2.0 · standard U9 shown

items.notes: 295 mph (474.8 km/h) one-way on 2022-05-14 at Johnny Bohmer Proving Grounds (ex-Shuttle runway), owner Larry Caplin in chassis #001; two Racelogic VBOX units installed by Racelogic's technician, independent observer Robert Mitchell. Two-way average 282.9 mph (455.3 km/h) on 2021-01-17 at Kennedy Space Center. The 2020 claim of 316/331 mph was withdrawn by SSC and is NOT used. Cross-check differs 4.1% because it is the two-way average (different measure).

insights.text: Every speed here carries a label: 15 independently VERIFIED runs and 15 makers' CLAIMS.
Just out: McLaren P1, Ferrari F80 and McLaren W1, all rated at exactly 350 km/h.
Only 3 of these 30 cars are fully electric, and two set their records in 2025.
Not ranked yet: the Bugatti Tourbillon (445 km/h claimed) isn't in customers' hands.
Chiron 300+ customer cars are capped at 440 km/h; the 490 run used a pre-production car.
By Guinness rules the record is still the Tuatara's 455 km/h two-way average (2021).

scope_note: Ranking: fastest one-way run timed by an independent body (VERIFIED: Racelogic, TUV, Guinness, FMSCI) or the maker's own figure (CLAIMED). The official Guinness-style two-way record is the SSC Tuatara's 455 km/h (2021); two-way averages are shown on the cards. Design targets and simulations are not counted. Cars: street-legal series production, 10+ built, deliveries started by Nov 2026; one card per model. Country = brand origin.

layout.image_prefer: the exact model and version, whole car visible, three-quarter front or side view, sharp, outdoor, real photograph (no renders, no CGI, no configurator images); landscape is fine
